    "Use Tukey's HSD (Honestly Significant Difference) test for all pairwise comparisons among the five paradigms to control the family-wise error rate.",
    "For 'Success', if using ANOVA, apply Tukey-Kramer; if using Chi-Square, perform pairwise comparisons of proportions with Bonferroni correction.",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., eta-squared or Cohen's d for pairwise) to quantify the magnitude of differences between paradigms."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham is expected to show significantly worse performance (higher Time-to-Target, lower Success, lower Path Efficiency, lower Speed, higher AD) compared to Combined, based on the summary means (Sham Success=0.27 vs Combined=0.78).",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only are expected to show intermediate performance between Sham and Combined.",
    "Bright Visual Only may show performance closer to Sham or Intermediate, given the lower n and mean Success (0.78) is high but n is small; however, the mean Success for Bright Visual Only (0.78) is higher than Sham (0.27) but lower than Combined (0.78) - wait, Combined is 0.779, Bright is 0.784. They are similar. ICMS (0.68) and Dim (0.67) are lower.",
    "Time-to-Target is expected to be significantly longer for Sham (4.68) compared to all others.",
    "AD (angular dispersion) is expected to be highest for Sham (0.236) and lowest for Dim Visual Only (0.335), indicating better directional control in visual-only conditions compared to Sham."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The provided data summary aggregates counts across 8 mouse levels. If the same mice were tested across multiple paradigms (repeated measures), a standard One-Way ANOVA is inappropriate and ignores within-mouse correlation. A Mixed-Effects Model with 'Mouse' as a random effect would be required.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary; while ANOVA is robust for balanced designs, the Chi-Square test is more appropriate for proportion comparisons.",
    "Extreme skewness in 'Time-to-Target' (max 201 vs mean 2.8) may violate normality assumptions, potentially requiring a non-parametric alternative like the Kruskal-Wallis test.",
    "Unequal sample sizes (Sham n=3505 vs Combined n=48846) increase the risk of Type I errors if variances are unequal (heteroscedasticity)."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Perform a Mixed-Effects Model (Linear Mixed Model for continuous variables, GLMM for Success) with 'Stim Paradigm' as a fixed effect and 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for potential repeated measures across the 8 mouse levels, followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons with p-value adjustment."
